PREFACE
This Code constitutes a codification of the general and permanent ordinances of the City of Social Circle, Georgia.
Source materials used in the preparation of the Code were the 2014 Code, as supplemented through 2016, and ordinances subsequently adopted by the city council. The source of each section is included in the history note appearing in parentheses at the end thereof. By use of the comparative tables appearing in the back of this Code, the reader can locate any section of the 2014 Code, as supplemented, and any subsequent ordinance included herein.
The various sections within each chapter have been catchlined to facilitate usage. Notes which tie related sections of the Code together and which refer to relevant state law have been included.
Chapter and Section Numbering System
The chapter and section numbering system used in this Code is the same system used in many state and local government codes. Each section number consists of two parts separated by a dash. The figure before the dash refers to the chapter number, and the figure after the dash refers to the position of the section within the chapter. Thus, the second section of chapter 1 is numbered 1-2, and the first section of chapter 6 is 6-1. Under this system, each section is identified with its chapter, and at the same time new sections can be inserted in their proper place by using the decimal system for amendments. For example, if new material consisting of one section that would logically come between sections 6-1 and 6-2 is desired to be added, such new section would be numbered 6-1.5. New articles and new divisions may be included in the same way or, in the case of articles, may be placed at the end of the chapter embracing the subject, and, in the case of divisions, may be placed at the end of the article embracing the subject. The next successive number shall be assigned to the new article or division. New chapters may be included by using one of the reserved chapter numbers.
Page Numbering System
The page numbering system used in this Code is a prefix system. The letters to the left of the colon are an abbreviation which represents a certain portion of the volume. The number to the right of the colon represents the number of the page in that portion. In the case of a chapter of the Code, the number to the left of the colon indicates the number of the chapter. In the case of an appendix to the Code, the letter immediately to the left of the colon indicates the letter of the appendix. Index
The index has been prepared with the greatest of care. Each particular item has been placed under several headings, some of which are couched in lay phraseology, others in legal terminology, and still others in language generally used by local government officials and employees. There are numerous cross references within the index itself which stand as guideposts to direct the user to the particular item in which the user is interested.
Looseleaf Supplements
A special feature of this publication is the looseleaf system of binding and supplemental servicing of the publication. With this system, the publication will be kept up to date. Subsequent amendatory legislation will be properly edited, and the affected page or pages will be reprinted. These new pages will be distributed to holders of copies of the publication, with instructions for the manner of inserting the new pages and deleting the obsolete pages.
Keeping this publication up to date at all times will depend largely upon the holder of the publication. As revised pages are received, it will then become the responsibility of the holder to have the amendments inserted according to the attached instructions. It is strongly recommended by the publisher that all such amendments be inserted immediately upon receipt to avoid misplacing them and, in addition, that all deleted pages be saved and filed for historical reference purposes.

The publisher is most grateful to Susan M. Roper, City Clerk, for her cooperation and assistance during the progress of the work on this publication. It is hoped that her efforts and those of the publisher have resulted in a Code of Ordinances which will make the active law of the city readily accessible to all citizens and which will be a valuable tool in the day-to-day administration of the city's affairs.

THE COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SOCIAL CIRCLE HEREBY ORDAINS, that the "City Code of Social Circle, Georgia" be designated as "City Code of Social Circle, Georgia 2017," and is hereby adopted as the Official Code of the City of Social Circle, Georgia pursuant to the authority of Section 2.25 of the Charter of the City of Social Circle, Georgia as enacted by the General Assembly of Georgia.

ORDINANCE NO. 2018-5
AN ORDINANCE ADOPTING AND ENACTING A NEW CODE FOR THE OFFICIAL CODE OF THE CITY OF SOCIAL CIRCLE, GEORGIA; PROVIDING FOR THE REPEAL OF CERTAIN ORDINANCES NOT INCLUDED THEREIN; PROVIDING A PENALTY FOR THE VIOLATION THEREOF; PROVIDING FOR THE MANNER OF AMENDING SUCH CODE; AND PROVIDING WHEN SUCH CODE AND THIS ORDINANCE SHALL BECOME EFFECTIVE.
BE IT ORDAINED BY THE:
Section 1. The Code entitled the "Official Code of the City of Social Circle, Georgia," published by Municipal Code Corporation, consisting of chapters 1 through 17, each inclusive, is adopted.
Section 2. All ordinances of a general and permanent nature enacted on or before Feb. 20, 2018, and not included in the Code or recognized and continued in force by reference therein, are repealed.
Section 3. The repeal provided for in section 2 hereof shall not be construed to revive any ordinance or part thereof that has been repealed by a subsequent ordinance that is repealed by this ordinance.
Section 4. Unless another penalty is expressly provided, every person convicted of a violation of any provision of the Code or any ordinance, rule or regulation adopted or issued in pursuance thereof shall be punished by a fine not to exceed $1,000.00, or by confinement for a maximum term not to exceed six months, or both. Each act of violation and each day upon which any such violation shall continue or occur shall constitute a separate offense. The penalty provided by this section, unless another penalty is expressly provided, shall apply to the amendment of any Code section, whether or not such penalty is reenacted in the amendatory ordinance. In addition to the penalty prescribed above, the City may pursue other remedies such as abatement of nuisances, injunctive relief and revocation of licenses or permits.
Section 5. Additions or amendments to the Code when passed in such form as to indicate the intention of the City to make the same a part of the Code shall be deemed to be incorporated in the Code, so that reference to the Code includes the additions and amendments.
Section 6. Ordinances adopted after Feb. 20, 2018, that amend or refer to ordinances that have been codified in the Code shall be construed as if they amend or refer to like provisions of the Code.
Section 7. This ordinance shall become effective October 16, 2018.
Passed and adopted by the City Council this 16 th day of October, 2018.

In the construction of this Code the following rules shall be observed, unless such construction would be inconsistent with the manifest intent of the council:
(1) General rule. All words and phrases shall be construed and understood according to the common and approved usage of the language; but technical words and phrases and such others as may have acquired a peculiar and appropriate meaning in the law shall be construed and understood according to such peculiar and appropriate meaning.
(2) Delegation of authority. Whenever this Code requires the head of a department or other officer of the city to do some act or perform some duty, it shall be construed to authorize subordinates to do the required act or perform the required duty unless the terms of the Code require otherwise.
(3) Computation of time. The time within which an act is to be done as provided in this Code or in any order issued thereunder, when expressed in days, shall be computed by excluding the first day and including the last, except if the last day is Sunday or a holiday it shall be excluded; when any such time is expressed in hours, Sunday, from midnight to midnight, shall be excluded.
(4) Overlapping provisions. Where any provision of this Code imposes greater restrictions upon the subject matter than any general provisions imposed by this Code, the provision imposing the greater restriction or regulation shall be applicable.
(Former § 1-003(2.))

(a) Violations. Except as otherwise provided herein, any person who violates the Code shall be guilty of a misdemeanor, and may be prosecuted in the city court.
(b) Penalties.
(1) Penalties specified by Code section. The monetary and/or civil penalties to be imposed upon persons who violate the Code are specified within the individual sections of this Code, except as otherwise established by the council or by law.
(2) Penalty where no penalty provided. Any person who violates this Code for which no penalty has been set forth shall, upon conviction, be subject to punishment by a fine not to exceed $1,000.00, or by confinement for a maximum term not to exceed six months, or both.

(a) The council shall hold regular meetings on the third Tuesday of each month at 6:30 p.m., unless otherwise ordered by the council; provided, that the mayor may convene the council whenever, in his opinion, the public business requires it, and he shall do so upon the application of three members of the council. Per the Georgia Sunshine Laws, 2012 Rewrite, HB 397, Open and Public Meetings Act (O.C.G.A. §§ 50-14-1 et seq.) and the Open Records Act (O.C.G.A. §§ 50-18-70 et seq.), the following apply: The meeting agenda will be available to the general public a reasonable time before the meeting, and a notice containing such information will be posted and maintained in a conspicuous place available to the public at the regular meeting place and on any city website at least one week prior to the meeting. The agenda shall list all items to be considered and briefly state what action is requested. All items timely submitted by city officials and staff to be on the agenda shall be placed on the agenda, and no one shall prohibit such a timely request from appearing on the agenda. Public requests to have an agenda item require clearly advising the clerk of the nature and details of the item including a summary of their position, and to provide all supporting documentation to be referenced in the meeting. To appear on a regular monthly meeting's agenda, the item must be submitted to the clerk by 1:00 p.m. on Tuesday of the week prior to the meeting. The agenda, together with data, reports, and memoranda, should be sent early enough to reach each member at least three days before the meeting. Any item received after the deadline will be held over for the next meeting unless a majority present at the meeting vote to add it to the agenda. Failure to include on the agenda an item which becomes necessary to address during the course of a meeting shall not preclude considering and acting upon such item. Public requests are to be added to the agenda as Item IV of the agenda titled, "Citizen Request."
(b) For specially called meetings, the agenda shall consist only of the item or items specifically indicated as the purpose of the called meeting. When any called meeting is to be held, the city will give due notice thereof, the posting of a written notice for at least 24 hours at the place of regular meetings and giving of written or oral notice at least 24 hours in advance of the meeting to the legal organ in the county where regular meetings are held and, upon written request from any local broadcast or print media outlet whose place of business and physical facilities are located in the county, notice by telephone or facsimile to that requesting media outlet at least 24 hours in advance of the called meeting. When special circumstances occur and are so declared by the mayor and council at the meeting, they may hold an emergency meeting with less than 24 hours' notice upon giving such notice of the meeting and subjects expected to be considered at the meeting as is reasonable under the circumstances including notice to said legal organ, in which event the reason for holding the meeting within 24 hours and the nature of the notice shall be recorded in the minutes. Any oral notice required or permitted by this subsection may be given by telephone. A summary of the subjects acted on and those members present at a meeting shall be written and made available to the public for inspection within two business days of the adjournment of a meeting.
(c) The minutes of any meeting shall be promptly recorded and such records (other than executive session minutes) shall be open to public inspection. Said minutes shall, at a minimum, include the names of the members present at the meeting, a description of each motion or other proposal made, and a record of all votes, who voted for and against. Official minutes of the meetings shall be maintained in the city hall. Copies of contracts, maps, or similar material or documents related to actions taken may be included in the minutes, or incorporated by reference to an alternate location, in which case, such documents shall be stored in a central location identified by ordinance or resolution.
(d) Open records shall be maintained per the state Records Retention Act, O.C.G.A. §§ 50-18-90 et seq. See O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(a). Records must be produced within three business days of an open records request if possible. If not, the response must be made within three business days as to when the records will be produced, O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(b)(1)(A). Requests must be made in writing. O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(b)(1)(B). All written requests shall go to a records custodian, O.C.G.A. § 50-18-71(b)(1)(B), the city clerk. All open records requests are subject to the regulations stated in the Open Records Act. O.C.G.A. 50-18-70, et seq.

Pursuant to the powers granted in accordance with the constitution and the laws of Georgia, the position of city manager was created by an amendment to the Charter of the city to carry out the duties and responsibilities of an administrative nature. The city manager shall have the following duties and responsibilities: To promote, facilitate and enforce this Code and all other city ordinances, resolutions, laws, regulations and rules; to coordinate matters and communications between the mayor and council and department heads of the city; to keep the mayor and council fully and regularly advised as to the financial condition and needs of the city and maintain accurate records reflecting the city's financial affairs; to assemble city department budget requests and present a compilation of same, along with an annual budget recommendation, to the mayor and council; to inspect, coordinate and represent the city in the performance of contracts and purchase of materials and supplies for the city within limitations and under such rules and regulations as may be imposed by the council; to prepare advertisements for bids and compile bids for contracts and purchases subject to any competitive bidding requirements; to maintain an inventory and maintenance schedule for city property; to coordinate, advise and recommend to the mayor and council in matters of personnel and compensation; to perform such other duties and responsibilities as may be delegated by the mayor and council; and to hold no other office or employment for remuneration while so engaged.

The public trust requires public servants to fulfill their duties faithfully and honestly and to subordinate any personal interest which conflicts with the public interest. A public servant is a trustee of the people and should strive to further the general welfare and not use public office or position to unethically improve his or her own private standing. The principal policies that form the foundation of this code of ethics are as follows:
(1) The trust of citizens in their government is cultivated when individual public servants act with integrity and when the public is aware that its servants act with integrity.
(2) The constitutions, laws and regulations of the United States and the State of Georgia and ordinances of the city should be upheld as a minimum standard of conduct.
(3) The most effective way to eradicate unethical practices is consistently to act with the highest moral principles and react appropriately to the ethical decisions of others.

As used in this section, the following words shall have the meaning ascribed to them below (unless otherwise required by context):
Benefit means anything of monetary value that a reasonably prudent person would recognize as being likely to be intended to influence a city official or employee in the performance or non-performance of an official action.
City official means the mayor, city council members, appointed officials, members of appointed boards, commissions and authorities.
Immediate family means spouse, child, parent or sibling of a city official.
Incidental interest means an interest in a person, entity or property which is not a substantial interest as defined herein and which has insignificant value.
Remote interest means an interest of a person or entity, including a city official, which would be affected in the same way as the general public. For example, the interest of an official in the property tax rate, general city fees, city utility charges or a comprehensive zoning ordinance or similar matters is deemed remote to the extent that the official would be affected in common with the general public.
Substantial interest means an interest, either directly or through a member of the immediate family, in another person or entity, where:
(1) The interest is ownership of five percent or more of the voting stock, shares or equity of the entity or ownership of $5,000.00 or more of the equity or market value of the entity; or
(2) The funds received by the person from the other person or entity during the previous 12 months either equal or exceed:
a. $5,000.00 in salary, bonuses, commissions or professional fees, or $5,000.00 in payment for goods, products or services, or
b. Ten percent of the recipient's gross income during that period, whichever is less;
c. The person serves as a corporate officer or member of the board of directors or other governing board of a for-profit entity other than a corporate entity owned or created by the mayor and city council; or

Except as otherwise provided in this section, Roberts' Rules of Order Newly Revised shall govern the conduct of council meetings. Except as otherwise provided, Roberts' Rules of Order Newly Revised shall be a general guide for meetings. Prior to each meeting, each member should: Study the data, reports, and memoranda accompanying the agenda; review his/her own research and observations on the issues, as well as pertinent ordinances; review alternative solutions to each problem; look for the best solution, determine what positions others are likely to take, and consider where and how much he or she is willing to compromise; be ready to discuss his or her position. The performance of the presiding officer is the key to effective, businesslike meetings. He or she sees that meetings are orderly, conducted per the rules of procedure, and that they progress at an appropriate speed. At the same time, the presiding officer is responsible for ensuring members and citizens have ample opportunity to express their views. Members share with the presiding officer the responsibility for properly conducted meetings. This includes having respect for one another's views. It also requires willingness to compromise, where possible, for the good of the city.
(1) Call to order. The mayor, or in his absence the mayor pro tempore, shall take the chair at the hour appointed for meeting, and shall immediately call the council to order.
(2) Roll call. Before proceeding with the business of the council, the city clerk or a deputy may call the roll of the members. The names of those present shall be entered in the minutes.
(3) Quorum. A majority of all the members of the council shall constitute a quorum at any meeting of the council, and an affirmative vote of a majority shall permit the conduct of all business except that for which a greater vote has been mandated by this Code or general law.
(4) Order of business. The business of the council shall generally be taken up for consideration and disposition in the following order: call to order by presiding officer; roll call; approval of minutes of previous meetings; petitions and communications; reports of standing committees; reports of special committees; unfinished business; new business; adjournment.
(5) Reading of minutes. Unless a reading of the minutes of a council meeting is requested by a member of the council, such minutes may be approved without a reading if the clerk has previously furnished each member with a copy thereof.
(6) Reports by committees. Any business coming before the council may be referred to the proper committee for investigation and report. It shall be the duty of such committee to examine all matters referred to such committee, and make a report thereof at the next regular meeting of the council, or show good cause why no report is made. Such reports shall not be in writing unless so directed by the presiding officer.

(a) Purpose. This article is created by the mayor and city council of the City of Social Circle, Georgia (hereinafter referred to as "mayor and council") to provide an organizational structure for the joint participation of private and public interests in the economic development of the business district of the city. The Main Street commission is further charged with raising and overseeing the use of contributed private capital through deductible charitable contributions to the city given for the dedicated purpose of paying for Main Street program initiatives within the Main Street district.
(b) Creation, appointment and compensation. A commission of the city is hereby created by official action of the mayor and council. The commission shall be the exclusive board of directors of the Main Street program whose title shall be "Social Circle Main Street Commission" (hereinafter referred to as the "Main Street commission"). The registered office of the Main Street commission shall be City Hall in the City of Social Circle with the address of P.O. Box 310, Social Circle, Georgia. The operational office of the Main Street commission shall be the Social Circle Visitors Center. This entity is a subsidiary commission of the city and all contributions to this organization shall be deemed gifts to the city and deductible under the current statues and regulations of the Internal Revenue Code. All financial accounts of the Main Street commission shall be deemed public funds, subject to the annual review of the auditors of the city and shall be maintained under the standards of fund accounting for cities required under the Official Code of Georgia for cities.
(1) Membership, qualifications and terms of office. The Main Street commission shall consist of eight voting members, each of whom shall serve a maximum term of three years. One commissioner shall serve as the representative of the Downtown Development Authority ("DDA") and be appointed by the DDA, and who will have the authority to participate in discussions and vote and be counted toward a quorum. Seven other members of the commission shall be appointed by the mayor and council. In addition to the voting members, one commissioner shall serve as the representative of the Historical Preservation Commission ("HPC") and be appointed by the HPC, and who will have the authority to participate in discussions, but not vote or be counted toward a quorum. One commissioner shall serve as a representative of the Social Circle City Schools ("school") and shall be appointed by the school board, and who will have the authority to participate in discussions, but not vote or be counted toward a quorum. The mayor of the city and the city manager shall serve as the city representatives to the commission with the authority to participate in discussions, but not vote or be counted toward a quorum. To ensure continuity of the Main Street commission, the initial terms are staggered as such: (1) Three voting members appointed by mayor and city council will serve until January 2025, (2) two voting members appointed by mayor and city council will serve until January 2026, and (3) two voting members appointed by mayor and city council will serve until January 2027.
(2) Appointment, vacancies and removal.
a. When appointing Main Street commission members, the city clerk shall take action as may reasonably be required to inform city residents, business owners in the Main Street district and property owners in the Main Street district that an opening exists on the Main Street commission. The city clerk shall accept applications from interested individuals. The mayor and council shall nominate individuals for confirmation. Confirmation shall be by a majority vote of the mayor and city council.
b. If a member is unable to complete a term of office, then an appointment to fill the unexpired term shall be made in the same manner as making an initial appointment. A member so appointed shall serve the remainder of the unexpired term of his or her predecessor.
c. If a member is absent from three regular meetings of the commission in a calendar year, without a Main Street commission approved excuse, the offending commissioner may be subject to being removed and replaced by official action of the mayor and council after a written request is made by the Main Street commission seeking removal of the absent commissioner. Members may participate via teleconference, with the approval of Main Street, if they are unable to attend a meeting, so long as a quorum is present. Industry appointees may send a substitute if they are unable to attend a Main Street meeting.
(3) Members shall serve without compensation, but may be reimbursed for reasonable expenses as approved by the mayor and council.
(c) Powers and duties. The Main Street commission shall:
(1) Make an annual report to the mayor and council on the economic condition of the Main Street district;
(2) Make recommendations to the mayor and council on economic and development issues concerning the city's business district;
(3) Search for local, state, federal, and private grants and other funds for the economic development of the Main Street district;
(4) To budget, invest, and when dedicated funds are held by others for the Main Street program, to oversee the budgeting and investment of such funds contributed to the Main Street program including, but not limited to, the funds held by Social Circle Main [Street commission.]
(5) To generally carry on, conduct, promote, operate and undertake any transaction or operation necessary to carry out the powers and duties outlined herein.
(6) To make all records available and assist the city auditor in the financial review of all contributions, public expenditures, investments, revenues and expenditures of the Main Street commission.
(7) To conduct all meetings subject to the notices and terms of the Georgia Open Meetings Law and to keep and make available all records, minutes and other written items, including communications, for review and copying pursuant to the Georgia Open Records Law.
(d) Assistance by the city. The city, through the action of the mayor and council, shall provide technical and clerical assistance as the Main Street commission by maintaining a permanent and complete record of the activities of the Main Street commission in the records of the clerk of the city. The mayor and council may appoint a downtown director to oversee the Main Street commission and its business.
(e) Bylaws, officers and quorum. The Main Street commission shall have the authority to supplement the ordinance from which this section derives by adopting rules and procedures, such as bylaws, for the transaction of its business. However, the Main Street commission's bylaws may not conflict with this section and if the bylaws do conflict, this section takes precedent. The Main Street commission shall have the prerogative to adopt reasonable rules and bylaws without amendment to this section or the vote of the mayor and council. The Main Street commission shall provide for the time and place of regular meetings and a method for the calling of special meetings. The Main Street commission shall meet at least six times in a calendar year. Meetings and notices of meetings shall be conducted in accordance with the Georgia Open Meeting and Records Act, O.C.G.A. § 50-18-70.
(1) A quorum shall consist of a majority of the current appointed and voting members. A vote of a majority of the members attending the meeting is needed to take action.
(2) The Main Street commission shall elect a chair and such other officers as it deems appropriate from among its members. Officers shall serve one-year terms and shall be eligible for reelection. The Main Street commission shall elect its initial officers at the first meeting following their appointment and thereafter in February of each year.

The two primary procurement methods for the city shall be competitive sealed bidding and competitive sealed proposals. All procurements shall be made via one of these two methods unless the procurement falls under the sole source procurement, or emergency procurement sections above, which serve as exceptions to these two primary methods. The terms and conditions of the purchasing section of the financial policies of the current budget are incorporated into this article as Schedule 1 attached to Ord. No. 2017-21 and incorporated herein by reference.
(1) Competitive sealed bidding. An invitation for bids shall be issued and shall include specifications, and all contractual terms and conditions applicable to the procurement. Adequate public notice of the invitation for bids shall be given a reasonable time, not less than 15 calendar days prior to the date set forth therein for the opening of bids. The public notice shall state the place, date, and time of bid opening. Bids shall be opened publicly in the presence of one or more witnesses at the time and place designated in the invitation for bids. The amount of each bid and such other relevant information as the city manager deems appropriate shall be recorded. The record and each bid shall be open to public inspection.
Bids shall be unconditionally accepted without alteration or correction, except as authorized in this article. Bids shall be evaluated based on the requirements set forth in the invitation for bids—no other criteria may be used in bid evaluation. Such requirements may include criteria to determine acceptability such as inspection, testing, quality, workmanship, delivery, and suitability for a particular purpose.
Correction or withdrawal of inadvertently erroneous bids before or after bid opening, or cancellation of awards or contracts based on such bid mistakes, may be permitted where appropriate. Mistakes discovered before bid opening may be modified or withdrawn by written notice received in the office designated in the invitation for bids prior to the time set for bid opening. After bid opening, no changes in bids shall be permitted unless the bidder can show by clear and convincing evidence that a mistake of a nonjudgmental character was made, the nature of the mistake, and the bid price actually intended. In lieu of bid correction, a low bidder alleging a material mistake of fact may be permitted to withdraw its bid if: (1) the mistake is clearly evident on the face of the bid document but the intended correct bid is not similarly evident, or (2) the bidder submits evidence which clearly and convincingly demonstrates that a mistake was made. All decisions to permit correction or withdrawal of bids shall be supported by written determination by a city official.
The contract shall be awarded with reasonable promptness by appropriate written notice to the lowest responsible and responsive bidder whose bid meets the requirements and criteria set forth in the invitation for bids. In the event the low responsive and responsible bid for a given project exceeds available funds as certified by the appropriate fiscal officer, the city manager is authorized, when time or economic considerations preclude re-solicitation of work of a reduced scope, to negotiate an adjustment of the bid price with the low responsive and responsible bidder, in order to bring the bid within the amount of available funds.
(2) Competitive sealed proposals. When the city manager, or other relevant department head, determines that the use of competitive sealed bidding is either not practicable or not advantageous to the city, a contract may be entered into by use of the competitive sealed proposals method.
As provided in a request for proposals, discussions may be conducted with responsible offerors who submit proposals determined to be reasonably susceptible of being selected for award for the purpose of clarification to assure full understanding of, and conformance to, the solicitation requirements.
Award shall be made to the responsible offeror whose proposal is determined in writing to be the most advantageous to the city, taking into consideration price and the evaluation factors set forth in the request for proposals. No factors other than those set forth in the request for proposals may be used in the evaluation.
(Ord. No. 2017-21, § 7, 9-19-2017)

(a) Occupation tax required for business dealings in Social Circle. For the year 2004 and thereafter, each person engaged in any business, trade, profession, or occupation in the incorporated area of Social Circle, Georgia, including an out-of-state business with no location in Georgia exerting substantial efforts within the state pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 48-13-7, shall pay an occupation tax for said business, trade, profession, or occupation. Registration of payment of such tax shall be displayed conspicuously in the taxpayer's place of business. If the taxpayer has no permanent business location in Social Circle, such business tax registration shall be shown to the city clerk or to any officer of the Walton County Sheriff's Department or a representative of the city department of public safety, upon request. Payment of occupation tax shall not be a precondition to the operation of any business or practice of any profession in the city, said tax being for raising revenue.
(b) Construction of terms; definitions.
Administrative fee means the approximate reasonable cost of handling and processing the occupation tax.
Employee means an individual whose work is performed under the direction and supervision of the employer and whose employer withholds FICA, federal income tax, or state income tax from such individual's compensation or whose employer issues to such individual for purposes of documenting compensation a form I.R.S. W-2 but not a form I.R.S. 1099.
Location or office shall include any structure or vehicle where a business, profession, or occupation is conducted, but shall not include a temporary or construction work site which serves a single customer or project or a vehicle used for sales or delivery by a business or practitioner of a profession.
Occupation tax means a tax levied on persons, partnerships, corporations, or other entities engaging in an occupation, profession, or business, for revenue raising purposes.
Regulatory fees means payments, whether designated as license fees, permit fees, or by another name, which are required by Social Circle as an exercise of its police power and as a part of or an aid to regulation of an occupation, profession, or business. The amount of a regulatory fee shall approximate the reasonable cost of the actual regulatory activity performed by Social Circle. A regulatory fee may not include an administrative fee.
Person includes sole proprietors, corporations, partnerships, or any other form of business organization, but excludes nonprofit organizations and state, federal or local governments or instrumentalities thereof.
Practitioner of profession or occupation is one who by law requires state licensure regulating such profession or occupation.
Practitioners of professions and occupations shall not include a practitioner who is an employee of a business, if the business pays an occupation tax.
(c) Administrative and regulatory fees.
(1) A non-prorated, non-refundable administrative fee of $100.00 shall be required on all business and occupation tax accounts for the initial start-up, renewal, or reopening of those accounts.
(2) Regulatory fees may only be imposed in compliance with O.C.G.A. § 48-13-9.
(d) Occupation tax levied; restrictions.
(1) An occupation tax shall be levied upon those businesses and practitioners of professions and occupations with one or more locations or offices in the incorporated area of Social Circle, based upon the following criteria:
a. The number of employees of the business or practitioner who are employed in the business or practitioner's dominant line of business in Social Circle. An employee who works for the same business or practitioner in more than one county or municipal corporation shall be counted as being employed in Social Circle if Social Circle is the local government entity in which the employee works for the longest period of time within the calendar year.
b. The number of employees of a business or practitioner includes all full-time positions and all full-time position equivalents as follows: An employee who works 40 hours or more weekly shall be considered a full-time position. The average weekly hours of employees who work less than 40 hours weekly shall be added and such sum shall be divided by 40 to determine the number of full-time position equivalents.
(2) Occupation tax schedule. The tax rate determined by number of employees for each business, trade, profession, or occupation is as follows and will be developed and updated from time to time by the mayor and council of the city: All businesses—$4.50 per employee.
(3) Exemptions.
a. No business or practitioner shall be required to pay more than one occupation tax for each of its locations.
b. No occupation tax shall be required from those real estate brokers, real estate agents, or real estate companies whose offices are located outside the jurisdiction and who sell property inside the jurisdiction.
c. No occupation tax shall be required from the following:
1. Any disabled veteran of any war or armed conflict in which any branch of the armed forces of the United States engaged, whether under United States command or otherwise;
2. Any blind person; or
3. Any veteran of peace-time service in the United States armed forces who has a physical disability incurred during the period of such service.
d. No occupation tax shall be levied on any state or local authority, nonprofit organization, or vendor operating under a contract with a tax-exempt agricultural fair, as that term is defined in O.C.G.A. § 2-2-8.
(e) Occupation tax on businesses with no location in Georgia.
(1) An occupation tax shall be levied on those businesses and practitioners of professions with no location or office in the state of Georgia if the business's largest dollar volume of business in Georgia is in the city and the business or practitioner: has one or more employees or agents who exert substantial efforts within Social Circle for the purpose of soliciting business or serving customers or clients; or owns personal or real property which generates income and which is located in Social Circle.
(2) The rate of taxation for businesses taxed under this section is the same as in subsection (d) above. For the purposes of computing the occupation tax on a business described in subsection (1) of this section, the number of employees of the business employed in Social Circle shall be computed based on the number of employees or agents who exert substantial efforts within the incorporated area of Social Circle for the purpose of soliciting business or serving customers or clients.
(f) Reduction for businesses commenced after July 1. When any person commences business on or after July 1 in any year, the occupation tax for the remaining portion of the year shall be 50 percent of the tax that would have been imposed for the entire year. A practitioner of a profession or occupation who elects as his or her occupation tax the amount described in subsection (h)(2) below shall receive no reduction in such amount.
(g) More than one place or line of business. Where a business is operated at more than one fixed location in Social Circle, each location shall be considered a separate business for the purpose of occupation tax. Such business is required to obtain the necessary registration and pay an occupation tax for each location.
(h) Professionals classified in O.C.G.A. § 48-13-9(c). Practitioners of professions as described in O.C.G.A. § 48-13-9(c)(1—18) shall elect as their occupation tax one of the following:
(1) The occupation tax based on number of employees as set forth in subsection (d) above.
(2) A fee of $100.00 per practitioner who is licensed to provide the service, such tax to be paid at the practitioner's office or location; provided, however, that a practitioner paying according to this paragraph shall not be required to provide information to the local government relating to the gross receipts of the business or practitioner. The per-practitioner fee applies to each person in the business who qualifies as a practitioner under the state's regulatory guidelines and framework.
(3) This election is to be made on an annual basis and must be done by January 1 each year. If no election is timely made, the occupation tax shall be imposed as set forth in subsection (d) above.
(i) Practitioners exclusively practicing for a government. Any practitioner whose office is maintained by and who is employed in practice exclusively by the US, Georgia, a city or county of Georgia or instrumentalities of the US, shall not be required to obtain a license or pay an occupation tax for that practice.
(j) Purpose and scope of tax. The occupation tax levied herein is for revenue, not for regulatory purposes, nor is the payment of the tax a condition precedent to the practice of any such profession, trade, or calling. The occupation tax only applies to those businesses and occupations covered by O.C.G.A. §§ 48-13-5—48-13-28. All other businesses and occupations are taxed by the local government pursuant to the pertinent general and/or local law and ordinance. This section does not apply to state or local authorities or non-profit organizations.
(k) Return required. The owner, proprietor, manager, or secretary of any business subject to the occupation tax for the upcoming calendar year shall, on or before December 31 of the preceding year, file with the city clerk, on a form furnished by the city clerk, a signed return setting forth each location at which business is conducted in Social Circle, the line or lines of business that the business conducts at each such location, the business tax identification number, the employees' social security numbers, and the number of employees of the business or practitioner, computed according to the above guidelines, for each line of business at each location. Any omission of federal tax identification number or social security number shall be reported to the state revenue commissioner. Where a business or practitioner has commenced operation after January 1, the return shall be filed no later than 30 days after commencement of such business.
(l) Failure to file return. Any person required to file an occupation tax return who fails to file by the date required shall be subject to a civil fine by a court of competent jurisdiction. The fine shall not exceed $200.00 and may be enforced by the contempt power of the court.
(m) Inspections of books and records; penalty for under-reporting. Social Circle, through its officers, agents, employees, or representatives, may inspect the books of the business for which the returns are made for the sole purpose of determining the number of employees of the business, and upon demand relevant books and records shall be made immediately available for such inspection. Failure to comply shall be punishable by a fine by a court of competent jurisdiction for the enforcement of city ordinances. The fine shall not exceed $200.00 and may be enforced by the contempt power of the court. Adequate records relevant to the number of employees of the business shall be kept in Social Circle for examination. If, after examination of the books or records, it is determined that a deficiency occurs as a result of under-reporting, the amount of the deficiency shall be treated as delinquent and shall be subject to the penalties and procedures for delinquent occupation tax amounts provided in subsections (o) through (r) below. This section shall not be construed as requiring any professional or business to divulge information protected under any privilege recognized by the laws of Georgia, including, but not limited to attorney-client privilege.
(n) Returns confidential. Except in judicial proceedings or other proceedings necessary to collect the occupation tax hereby levied, or as otherwise required by law, it shall be unlawful for any person to divulge or make known in any manner gross receipts set forth or disclosed in any occupation tax return required hereunder. Information revealing gross receipts shall be confidential and open only to the officials, employees, agents, or clerks of Social Circle using said returns for the purpose of this occupation tax levy and the collection of the tax. Independent auditors or bookkeepers retained by the city shall be classed as "employees". Nothing herein shall be construed to prohibit the publication by officials of statistics, so classified as to prevent the identification of gross receipts, or the inspection of information revealing gross receipts by duly qualified employees of the tax departments of the State of Georgia, the United States, and other local governments.
(o) When tax due; tax registration.
(1) Each occupation tax for 2004 and succeeding calendar years thereafter shall be payable January 31 of each year and shall, if not paid by May 1 of each year, be subject to penalties for delinquency as prescribed in subsection (p) below. If any person commences business for the first time in Social Circle after January 1, the tax shall be due and payable 30 days after the date of the commencement of the business, and delinquency shall occur upon nonpayment after 90 days from the due date.
(2) The tax registration herein provided for shall be issued by the city clerk upon receipt of all amounts due for the occupation tax. Each such registration shall be for the calendar year the registration was obtained unless otherwise specifically provided.
(p) Penalty for delinquency; interest on delinquent tax; other remedies.
(1) Should any occupation tax imposed by this chapter be delinquent, the person liable for the tax shall pay a penalty of ten percent of the tax due.
(2) Any occupation tax which becomes delinquent shall bear interest from the date of delinquency on the unpaid amount at 18 percent per annum.
(3) The city clerk may collect delinquent occupation taxes in the same manner as provided by law for tax executions.
(4) A court of competent jurisdiction for the enforcement of ordinances of Social Circle may impose a civil fine for failure to pay the occupation tax (or regulatory fee), not to exceed $500.00, which may be enforced by the contempt power of the court. Per City of Atlanta v. Barnes, this subsection (p)(4) shall not apply to attorneys.
(q) Registration to be revoked for failure to pay tax, file returns, permit inspection of books. Upon the failure of any business to timely pay occupation tax or to timely or truthfully make returns, or upon failure to amend a return to set forth the truth, or upon failure to permit inspection of its books as above provided, any business tax registration granted under this chapter shall be automatically revoked. No new business tax registration shall be granted for a business for which any part of the occupation tax is unpaid, or to a person who has failed to submit adequate records as requested by Social Circle in accordance with subsection (m). However, nothing in this section shall be construed as prohibiting the operation of any business or practice of any profession in Social Circle, regardless of status of the occupation tax registration for such business or professional.
(r) Lien for delinquent occupation tax.
(1) The city clerk and/or designated tax collector, upon any tax or installment becoming delinquent and remaining unpaid, shall issue execution for the amount of said tax and the penalty against the person liable for said tax, which said execution shall bear interest at the rate of 18 percent per annum from the date when such tax or installment becomes delinquent. The lien shall cover the property in Social Circle of the person liable for said tax, all as provided by the laws of the city and Georgia. The lien of said occupation tax shall become fixed on and date from the time when such tax or any installment thereof becomes delinquent.
(2) The execution shall be levied by the city clerk upon the property of the defendant in Social Circle, and sufficient property shall be advertised and sold to pay the amount of said execution, with interest and costs. All proceedings in relation thereto shall be as provided by the laws of Social Circle and Georgia, including without limitation O.C.G.A. tit. 48, chs. 3, 4 and 5.
(s) Reserved.
(t) Social circle officials; subpoena and arrest powers. Social Circle's duly designated officers and inspectors have full subpoena powers regarding enforcement hereof.
(u) Businesses licensed by state. Each person subject to the occupation tax which is also licensed by the state shall post the state license conspicuously in its place of business. This requirement is not a precondition to the operation of any business or practice of any profession in the city.
(v) Businesses not covered by this chapter. The following businesses are not subject to occupation tax, registration fees or regulatory fees provided for herein, but may be assessed other types of taxes pursuant to other general laws of Georgia or by local law:
(1) Those businesses regulated by the Georgia Public Service Commission.
(2) Those electrical service businesses organized under O.C.G.A. tit. 46, ch. 3.
(3) Any farm operation for the production from or on the land of agricultural products, but not including agribusiness.
(4) Cooperative marketing associations governed by O.C.G.A. § 2-10-105.
(5) Insurance companies governed by O.C.G.A. §§ 33-8-8, et seq.
(6) Motor common carriers governed by O.C.G.A. § 46-7-15.
(7) Those businesses governed by O.C.G.A. § 48-5-355. (Businesses that purchase carload lots of guano, meats, meal, flour, bran, cottonseed, or cottonseed meal and hulls.)
(8) Agricultural products and livestock raised in Georgia governed by O.C.G.A. § 48-5-356.
(9) Depository financial institutions governed by O.C.G.A. § 48-6-93.
(10) Facilities operated by a charitable trust governed by O.C.G.A. § 48-13-55.
(w) Occupation tax inapplicable where prohibited by law or provided for pursuant to other existing law. An occupation tax shall not apply where such levy is prohibited or exempted by the laws of Georgia or of the United States.
(x) Amendment, repeal of provision. This amendment shall be subject to amendment or repeal, in whole or part, and no such amendment or repeal shall be construed to deny the right of the city to assess and collect any of the taxes or other charges prescribed. Said amendment may increase or lower the amounts and tax rates of any occupation and may change the classification thereof.
(y) Applications of provisions to prior section 4-010. This amendment does not repeal or affect the force of any part of any ordinance heretofore passed where taxes levied under such Prior Code section 4-010 have not been paid in full. Any parts of ordinances or code sections heretofore and hereinafter passed which provided for the issuing and enforcing of execution for any tax or assessment required by such, or that imposed fines or penalties for the nonpayment of such tax, or for failure to pay regulatory fees provided for therein, or failure to comply with any other provisions hereof, shall continue and remain in force until such tax, regulatory fee, or assessment shall be fully paid.
(z) Enforcement of provisions. It is hereby made the duty of the city clerk to see that the provisions hereof relating to occupation taxes are observed.
(aa) Full force and effect until changed by governing body. This amendment shall remain in full force and effect until changed by amendment adopted by the mayor and council. All provisions hereto relating to any form of tax herein levied shall remain in full force and effect until such taxes have been paid in full.
(bb) Requirement of public hearing before tax increase. The council shall conduct at least one public hearing before increasing the rate of occupation tax set forth herein.
(cc) Public hearing in years of increasing revenue. In any year when revenue from occupation taxes is greater than revenue from occupation taxes for the preceding year, the mayor and council shall hold one or more public hearings as part of the process of determining how to use the additional revenue.
(dd) Exemption or reduction in occupation tax. The mayor and council may by subsequent amendment or resolution provide for an exemption or reduction in occupation tax to one or more types of businesses or practitioners of occupations or professions as part of a plan for economic development or attracting or encouraging selected types of businesses or practitioners of selected occupations or professions. Such exemptions or reductions in occupation tax shall not be arbitrary or capricious, and the reasons shall be set forth in the minutes of the mayor and council.
(ee) Conflicts between specific and general provisions. Where there is an apparent conflict in this amendment between specific and general provisions, the specific shall control.
(ff) Effective date. This amendment took effect on December 31, 2003.

(a) Definitions.
Dealer in second-hand merchandise means any private entity which holds itself or its place of business out as a buyer, seller or trader of used or distressed merchandise.
Licensee is deemed to include all persons, agents or employees operating under said license.
Pawnbroker means any private entity with which property is deposited as security for the payment of a debt.
Specific entities included in this section. Specifically included in the above defined categories shall be:
(1) Any dealer, salesperson, or buyer of gold, silver, jewelry, coins and/or other precious metals, whether said sales, trades or purchases are retail, wholesale or by any form of pawn;
(2) Any dealer, salesperson, or buyer of semi-precious metals to include, but not being limited to, iron, steel, copper, aluminum, brass, and wet-cell batteries, commonly referred to as "junk";
(3) Any dealer, salesperson, or buyer of used parts designed for use with automobiles, trucks or other vehicles; and
(4) Any private entity providing selling space, singularly or in multiple units, indoors or outdoors, for the purpose of what is commonly referred to or known as a flea market operation shall, for the purpose of this section, be considered a primary license applicant, and as such, shall be held responsible for the provisions of this section concerning transactions made by lessees of said selling space in the same manner as if said lessees were agents or employees.
Specific entities excluded in this section. Specifically excluded from the above defined categories shall be:
(1) Wholesalers, buyers and sellers, who sell, trade or deal only with retail mercantile establishments;
(2) Private sales, commonly referred to as garage sales, when held on the seller's residential property for a period not exceeding 24 hours;
(3) Organizational sales by non-profit groups holding fund raisers with all funds going directly to the sponsoring organization; and
(4) State licensed used car or truck dealers or repair garages as to the dealing in used vehicle parts.
(b) Licensing requirements.
(1) Application to be submitted. Any private entity desiring to do business as a pawnbroker or dealer in second-hand merchandise shall make application and notice to the city, at least 72 hours prior to the opening or advertising of the business operation.
(2) Application requirements. All notices/applications shall include the following: 1) full name and address of the person, company or corporation; and 2) submission of standard fingerprint cards of principals, agents and employees to the clerk within 24 hours of the application of agents or employees operating in the city. The cost of processing the fingerprinting shall be deposited.
(3) Fee required. At the time of submission of an application to operate as a pawnbroker or dealer in second-hand merchandise the applicant shall pay the annual license fee as specified in section 4-35 of this Code).
(c) Traveling or itinerant dealers.
(1) Provisions applicable to traveling dealers. All of the provisions of this section shall also apply to any traveling or itinerant dealer, his agent, or employees intending to establish a temporary business of a type addressed by this section.
(2) Exceptions and specifications. The license fee for an itinerant dealer shall be $25.00, and the license issued shall be valid for a period not to exceed seven calendar days. No itinerant dealer, his agent, or employee may apply for or receive a temporary license more than once during any calendar quarter. Any dealer, agent or employee not previously furnishing fingerprint cards as required by this section must do so within 24 hours of any subsequent application.
(d) General regulations.
(1) Business hours. No licensee shall open his place of business or conduct any business between 10:00 p.m. and 8:00 a.m.; provided, however, that such a place of business may remain open until 10:30 p.m. on Fridays and until 11:00 p.m. on Saturdays.
(2) Premises to be open to police. It shall be the duty of every licensee to admit to his premises the sheriff or any deputy or police officer or a representative of the city department of public safety, or agent of the city who may desire at any time to search for articles missing or stolen, or to make any inspection authorized by this section, without a search warrant.
(e) Records requirements.
(1) Forms to be used, distributed. Each licensee shall have an adequate supply of pre-numbered three-part forms which, in addition to any records deemed necessary by the licensee, must be made, maintained and distributed by the licensee daily. Specific retention and distribution of forms shall occur as follows:
a. The original shall be maintained by the licensee as a permanent record to be kept for a minimum of ten years;
b. The second copy of the form shall be kept in the Walton County Sheriff's files or the city department of public safety's files, for comparison with items reported stolen; and
c. The third copy will be forwarded by the Walton County Sheriff's Department or the city department of public safety, to the communications record center for G.C.I.C. comparison as computer time availability permits.
(2) Licensees to provide accurate descriptions of merchandise. The licensees shall enter an accurate description of all property pledged or sold to them. The description shall include as a minimum: The name of the maker of the article; any identifying mark or number; and a statement of the kind and color of material of which it is made.
(3) Licensees to provide accurate descriptions of seller or depositor. The licensees shall also enter positive identifying information of the person who sold or deposited the article, including name, address, date of birth, race, estimated weight and height, and signature. Licensees may take such information from a valid driver's license or other such official form bearing a photograph of the person when completing the form.
(4) Entries to be timely made. The entries required in subsection (e)(1) above shall be made at the time of the transaction. Other records maintained by the licensee shall be kept current to reflect every transaction and they shall be made as soon as possible following each transaction.
(5) False entries. It is unlawful for any licensee to make any false entry in any records required by this section.
(6) Transactions with minors prohibited. It shall be unlawful for any licensee to receive any article in pawn, or purchase any article for resale, from any person under 18 years of age.
(f) Holding of goods.
(1) Goods to be held for ten days. Any licensee operating under this section who takes any kind of personal property, on pawn or buys such, taking full title thereto, shall hold the property so taken in pawn or sale for at least ten days before disposing of the goods by sale, transfer, shipment, or otherwise.
(2) Exception. This aforesaid provision cannot be waived by contract, but it does not apply nor is it intended to cover purchasers from reputable wholesale supply houses and manufacturers, or goods of a perishable nature.
(3) Surrender of stolen property. If is reasonably suspected that any item bought, sold or traded to, or received in any manner by licensees, is the subject of any crime, the licensees shall, upon demand of the sheriff or his designee, or a representative of the department of public safety, surrender the same to the Walton County Sheriff's Department or the city department of public safety.
(g) General operating requirements for junk dealers and junk yards.
(1) Application of this subsection. The general operating requirements as specified herein shall apply to all junk dealers.
(2) Appearance of junk yards. The following appearance requirements shall apply to all junk dealers in Social Circle:
a. No weeds in a junk yard shall be permitted to attain a height of more than eight inches;
b. Junk shall be stored in piles not exceeding ten feet in height, and shall be arranged to permit easy access to all such junk for firefighting purposes;
c. The area on the premises where junk is kept shall be enclosed, except for entrances and exits, with a solid, vertical wall or fence of a minimum height of eight feet measured from ground level;
d. The fence or wall shall not contain any poster or advertising of any kind except one sign of the licensee not exceeding nine square feet in size; and
e. Entrances and exits shall not be wider or more numerous than reasonably necessary for conduct of the business.
(3) Sanitary conditions to be maintained. The following sanitary conditions shall be maintained at all junk dealers:
a. No junk yard shall be allowed to become a nuisance; nor shall any junk yard be operated in such manner as to become injurious to the health, safety, or welfare of the community or of any residents close by;
b. No water shall be allowed to stand in any place in such manner as to afford a breeding place for mosquitoes;
c. No garbage or other waste liable to give off a foul odor or attract vermin shall be kept on the premises; nor shall any refuse of any kind be kept on the premises, unless such refuse is saleable junk;
d. No junk shall be allowed become scattered or blown off the business premises;
e. No combustible material of any kind not necessary or beneficial to the business shall be kept on the premises; nor shall the premises be allowed to become a fire hazard;
f. Fuel and oil shall be removed from any scrapped engines or vehicles on the premise;
g. No junk or other material shall be burned on the premises in any incinerator not meeting the requirements of the city building codes; and no junk or other material shall be burned on the premises in the open; and
h. No noisy processing of junk or other noisy activity shall be carried on in connection with the licensed business on any Sunday holiday, or on any day between the hours of 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m.
(4) Administrative requirements. The licensee shall permit inspection of the premises by law enforcement at any reasonable time.
(h) Penalties. Any licensee or agent or employee thereof violating this section shall be subject to punishment as a misdemeanor by a fine not to exceed $1,000.00 or by confinement in the Walton County Jail or other detention facility for a maximum term not to exceed six calendar months, or both, at the discretion of the presiding judge.

(a) Definitions. The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Due date means from the 20th day after the close of the monthly period for which tax is to be computed.
Guestroom means a room occupied or intended, arranged or designed for occupancy, by one or more occupants for the purpose of living quarters or residential use.
Hotel means any structure or any portion of a structure, including but not limited to any bed and breakfast house, lodging-house, rooming-house, dormitory, Turkish bath, bachelor hotel, studio hotel, motel, motor hotel, auto court, inn, public club or private club, containing guestrooms and which is occupied or is intended or designed for occupancy, by guests, whether rent is paid in money, goods, labor or otherwise. Occupant means any person who, for a consideration, uses, possesses or has the right to use or possess any room in a hotel under any lease, concession, permit, right of access, license or use or other agreement or otherwise.

Rent means the consideration received for occupancy valued in money, whether received in money or otherwise, including all receipts, cash, credits, and property or services of any kind or nature, and also the amount for which credit is allowed by the operator to the occupant, without any deduction whatsoever.
Return means any return filed or required to be filed as provided in this article.
(b) Rate of levy. There is set and levied on each occupant of a guestroom of any hotel located within the corporate limits of this city a tax in the amount of five percent of rent for such occupancy. This tax is imposed per O.C.G.A. § 48-13-51(a)(1)(A)(3).
(c) Collection of tax by operator. It shall be the duty of every operator of a hotel located within the city to collect the tax on occupants imposed herein.
(d) Exemption. Notwithstanding any other provision of this article, no tax shall be imposed upon a permanent resident, or upon rooms, lodgings or accommodations for a period of one or more days for use by state or local government officials or employees traveling on official business.
(e) Registration of operator. Every person engaging in or about to engage in business as an operator of a hotel in this city shall immediately register the business with the city clerk, on a form provided by the city clerk for such purpose. The required registration shall set forth the name which the operator transacts business or intends to transact business, the location of his place of business, and such other information as would facilitate the collection of the tax by the city clerk. The registration shall be signed by the owner if a natural person, by a member or partner in case of ownership by association or partnership, or by an officer in the case of ownership by a corporation. A separate registration shall be required for each place of business of an operator.
(f) Certificate of taxing authority. Upon registration of an operator, the city clerk shall issue to such operator without charge a certificate of authority to collect the tax on occupants. Each certificate shall state the name and location of the business to which it relates.
(g) Due date and required report. All taxes levied by this article shall be due and payable to the city clerk monthly on or before the 20th day succeeding each respective month in which such taxes are collected, and payment shall be accompanied by a return for the preceding monthly period showing the gross rent, rent from permanent residents, taxable rent, and amount of tax collected or otherwise due for the period, and such other information as may be required by the city clerk.
(h) Collection fee allowed operators. Operators collecting the tax levied under this article shall be allowed a percentage of the tax due and accounted for and shall be reimbursed in the form of a deduction in submitting, reporting and payment of the amount due if the amount is not delinquent at the time of payment. The rate of the deduction shall be the same rate authorized for deductions from state tax under the "Georgia Retailers" and "Consumer's Sales and Use Tax Act".
(i) Determination if no return made; unsatisfactory return.
(1) Estimate authorized. If any hotel operator fails to file a return as required under the provisions of this article, the city clerk shall make an estimate of the amount of gross rentals of such operator for the period for which the operator failed to file the return and such estimate shall be based upon any information which is or may come into the possession of the city clerk. One or more deficiency determinations may be made of the amount due for one or more monthly periods.
(2) Notice of determination. The city clerk or his designated representative shall give to the hotel operator written notice of his determination as provided in this section. The notice may be served personally or by mail; if by mail, such service shall be addressed to the operator at his address as it appears in the records of the city clerk. Service by mail is complete when mailed by certified mail.
(3) Interest on amount found due. The amount of the determination made under this section shall bear interest at the rate of three-fourths of one percent per month, or fraction of a month, from the 20th day of the month following the monthly period for which the amount or any portion of the amount should have been returned until the date of payment.
(4) Time within which notice of deficiency determination to be mailed. Except in the case of failure to make a return, every notice of a deficiency determination shall be mailed within three years after the 20th day of the month following the monthly period in which the amount is proposed to be determined, or within three years after the return is filed, whichever period should expire last.
(5) Unsatisfactory return. The same rules shall apply if a return is made but is determined to be unsatisfactory by the city clerk.
(j) Required records. Each hotel operator collecting a tax under the provisions of this article shall keep all records, receipts, invoices and other pertinent papers for a period of at least three years, setting forth dates of occupancy and such other information as the city clerk may require.
(k) Administration and enforcement.
(1) Authority of the clerk. The city clerk shall administer and enforce the provisions of this article for the collection of the tax imposed by this article.
(2) Records required from operators; form. Every operator renting guestrooms in this city to a person shall keep such records, receipts, invoices and other pertinent papers in such form as the mayor and council may require.
(3) Examination of authorized records; audits. The city clerk or any person authorized in writing by the city clerk may examine the books, papers, records, financial reports equipment and other facilities of any operator renting guestrooms to a person and any operator liable for the tax, in order to verify the accuracy of any return made, or if no return is made by the operator, to ascertain and determine the amount required to be paid.
(4) Authority to require reports; contents. In administration of the provisions of this article, the city clerk may require the filing of reports by any persons or class of persons having in such persons' possession or custody information relating to rentals of guestrooms which are subject to the tax. The reports shall be filed with the city clerk when required by the city clerk and shall set forth the rental charged for each occupancy; the date of occupancy and such other information as the city clerk may require.
(l) Action for collection of tax.
(1) Action for tax; time for. At any time within three years after any tax or any portion of such tax required to be collected becomes due and payable, the mayor and council may bring an action in a court of competent jurisdiction in the name of the city to collect such amount due, together with interest, court fees, filing fees, attorney's fees and other incidental legal fees.
(2) Duty of successors or assignees of operator to withhold tax from purchase money. If any operator liable for any amount under this article sells his business or quits the business, his successors or assigns shall withhold sufficient of the purchase price to cover such amount until the former owner produces a receipt from the city clerk showing that he has been paid or a certificate showing no amount is due.
(3) Liability for failure to withhold, certificate of notice of amount due, time to enforce successor's liability. If the purchaser of a business fails to withhold the purchase price as required, he shall be personally liable for the payment of the amount required to be withheld by him to the extent of the purchase price.
(4) Tax credit, or interest paid more than once or erroneously or illegally collected. Whenever the amount of any tax or interest has been paid more than once, or has been erroneously or illegally collected or received by the city under this section, it may be offset by the city clerk.
(m) Penalties. Any operator or other person who fails to register as required in this articles or who fails to furnish any return required to be made, or who fails or refuses to furnish a supplemental return or other data required by the city clerk, or who renders a false or fraudulent return shall be deemed guilty of an offense and upon conviction shall be punished as provided herein.

The mayor and council have the power and authority to: Provide, own and furnish, in and near the city, cemeteries for the burial of the dead; regulate and control the interments in such cemeteries; exercise police control and to care for such cemeteries; and, provide city care to lots in such cemeteries. The mayor and council find that the historical and cultural heritage of the city is among its most valued and important assets and that the preservation of this heritage is essential to the promotion of the health, prosperity, and general welfare of the people of the city and of the public generally. The cemeteries, graveyards, and burial grounds are uniquely precious and vulnerable thus deserving of devoted stewardship; the city is richly blessed with the heritage and history of its people who are now deceased; that many native pioneers and early residents were integral to the community's development; and that the resting places and memorials of those who have passed are valuable to current and future generations. Therefore, with the intent of caring for and managing the cemeteries, graveyards, and burying grounds, and regulating the use of such areas for the utility, education, pleasure, and welfare of the citizens; the mayor and council hereby ordain and enact into law this amended cemetery chapter.
(1) Definitions. The following phrases, words and their derivations shall have the meaning given herein.
Municipal cemetery or cemetery is the municipal cemetery of the city, which includes Social Circle Cemetery East and Social Circle Cemetery West.
Person is any person, firm, partnership, association, corporation, company or organization of any kind.
Resident shall mean anyone who has or formerly had his/her main dwelling in the city and has or previously maintained such residence for at least 60 consecutive days prior to purchasing a burial plot in the municipal cemetery.
Superintendent is the utilities superintendent of the city.
(2) Authority. The superintendent shall manage, operate and maintain the municipal cemetery subject to any limitations and restrictions set forth herein or contained in any applicable laws.
(3) Rules and regulations. The council may establish rules and regulations for the use of the cemetery relating to: Subdividing the cemetery into burial plots; capacity of each plot; location of graves; and type of plantings, monuments and markers that will be permitted for the proper and most attractive development of the cemetery. These rules include without limitation the following:
a. The use of wire, iron stands, rocks, concrete containers, or breakable containers causes hazards to visitors, lawn maintenance personnel and machinery, and are strictly prohibited.
b. During the grass cutting season, between the first of March and the last of October, any flowers or floral arrangements, or any other items must be placed in the permanent vase on the flat marker. Any other types of flower or floral arrangement which cannot be put in these vases are not permitted.
c. No trinkets (small ceramic statuary, beads, crosses, lights, etc.) are allowed on any grave space or marker since these cause mowing and trimming hazards which may harm visitors and lawn maintenance personnel and machinery. The plot owner agrees to not attempt to establish a shrine to their loved one or around a grave, inurnment, or crypt.
d. The city reserves the right to:
1. Enter upon any area and remove any monument, effigy, structure, inscription, or other items placed on, upon or near any plot that is in violation of these rules and regulations. Any items removed will not be held for reclamation and will be deemed abandoned property and will be disposed of at the city's discretion. The city will have no liability for any loss or damage to any items placed on or near a plot in violation of these rules and regulations or removed by the city;
2. Remove floral arrangements that have become unsightly in the opinion of the city; and
3. Grade and improve all sections of the city cemetery.
e. The plucking of, or removal of, any plant or flower, either wild or cultivated, is strictly prohibited. Planting, mowing or maintenance of any kind by anyone other than the city or those whom are contracted by the city is strictly prohibited.
f. The city or any contract company for the city will not be held responsible for damages to any grave marker.
g. Any changes such as: address, phone number or ownership of family plot are the sole responsibility of the owner to notify the city of these changes.
